title: Bind the orchestrator settings to the typed approval policy
description:
CONSUMER EDGE for task-5d8f11c86a3a41b4a8a420ef0d52a444. Clause 1 requires this task to exist. This is the consumer closest to the incident that motivated the contract.

THE INCIDENT, stated exactly, because it is what this task prevents recurring. On 2026-08-15 the orchestrating board ran auto-approval on a 2s delay configured OUTSIDE any typed contract — a setting nobody had stated per unit of work. Every BLOCKED task was promoted to PLANNING inside a two-minute window, clearing each task's recorded blockedReason. Two were release-cutover tasks whose descriptions named an explicit human authority gate as a hard dependency: a GA activation record requiring GO_ACTIVATE, and a legacy quiesce drill requiring GO_QUIESCE. Neither GO had ever been issued — verified by scanning every message channel. Both became claimable under that 2s delay, so no human would have seen a plan before a worker began executing it.

WHAT LANDED (commit 18f0964, published from the @moe/core root, verify by grep before naming symbols):
- APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS, frozen: ["PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN", "REQUIRE_HUMAN"].
- ApprovalPolicy, a discriminated union whose PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN arm carries a REQUIRED delayMs. It is deliberately impossible to express an auto-approval policy without stating its delay — that is the whole point, and it is exactly the property the untyped setting lacked.
- decideApprovalAuthority, HumanAuthorityGate, grantHumanAuthority, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS.

SCOPE: decode the orchestrator's approval settings into a typed ApprovalPolicy, refusing rather than defaulting when the delay is absent or malformed. NOT IN SCOPE: the daemon wiring (task-5fcfdae58ec7419fbcba0000ef08d3b6), the control-room surface (task-6fcca7da2bc44194b36bb2454088a62b), or changing the contract.

DO NOT MAKE THE SETTING THE GATE. A blanket project-wide switch is what FAILED in the incident, and the contract's rails say so: fast delegation was the correct setting for most of that board, and flipping everything to manual review to protect two tasks is the wrong trade. This task binds the POLICY. The gate is per-unit-of-work and is not expressible in, or satisfiable by, a settings file — if the design lets a settings value approve gated work, the design is wrong.

A DECODE THAT DEFAULTS IS THE DEFECT. An absent delay must produce a refusal with a stable code, not a fallback value. `mem:pinned-value-is-a-decision-only-if-another-was-representable` — a decoder that cannot express "refuse" makes every decoded delay meaningless.
definitionOfDone: The orchestrator's approval settings decode into a typed ApprovalPolicy from @moe/core, with the decode reachable from the settings load path rather than only exported.

An absent, empty, or malformed auto-approval delay is REFUSED with an exact stable code and its layer, asserted literally - never defaulted to a fallback delay. A test proves the refusal is representable by showing a valid settings value decoding successfully in the same suite.

No settings value, or combination of them, approves gated work; a test enumerates every ApprovalPolicy member decodable from settings against a gated unit and asserts refusal for each, with a nonzero exact cardinality equal to the vocabulary size.

The settings binding introduces no project-wide switch that stands in for the per-unit-of-work gate, and a test asserts a gated unit stays refused under the most permissive settings the file can express.
A mutation drill making the decoder default an absent delay instead of refusing turns a named test red on its code-and-layer assertion, restored byte-exact and verified by hash.
reopenReason: Governor routing 01:48Z under the human's standing unblock directive. Premise re-verified minutes ago: grep for approvalMode/speedModeDelayMs in non-test daemon/package sources still returns zero — the claimed settings load path remains absent, so the old conclusion (no production-ready plan without an unattached decoder) still holds AS A WORKER conclusion. The ARCHITECT output it calls for is different: per the Clause-2 rail, measure the gap symbol by symbol and file the prerequisite production task(s) (the settings load/decode surface itself), then re-block this consumer on them by id — or, if fresh measurement finds the surface landed since HEAD ddb4753 under a different name, plan against it. Do not plan this binding task around the gap.
blockedReason:
Re-blocked by architect-27b64950 at HEAD abc3dcf, 2026-08-16 02:20Z. The governor asked me to file prerequisite task(s) or plan against a renamed surface. I am doing NEITHER, and that is the point: the gap is a missing DECISION, not a missing symbol.

MEASURED, both directions:
- `grep -rn "approvalMode\|speedModeDelayMs" --include=*.ts apps packages adapters` -> ZERO. Unchanged.
- `grep -rln "ProjectSettings|settingsDecode|decodeSettings|OrchestratorSettings"` -> ZERO. Nothing landed under another name.
- Both candidates measured AND RULED OUT, so nobody re-measures them a fourth time: `ProjectConfigurationSettings` / `parseProjectConfigurationSettings` (packages/contracts/.../project-configuration-contract.ts:154, parser.ts:186) is the PRODUCT manifest surface consumed by project-configuration-selection.ts for settingsDigest, carrying no approval mode. `WrapperKnobs` / `readWrapperKnobs` (orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts:9,32) are ENV knobs. Neither reaches transitional plan auto-approval, as architect-09b5f32a recorded.

WHY NO PREREQUISITE FILED. The real consumer runs in the sibling transitional daemon, and epic rail 2 pins development to moe-next. A moe-next-local loader would land with NO consumer here — the Clause-1 "exports the symbols is not composition" failure — and its owner could not satisfy their own consumer-edge DoD. Filing it would be guessing an answer only the human can give.

THE DECISION, unchanged from architect-09b5f32a and still unanswered: which repo/package owns the transitional settings load and auto-approval consumer, and how may it legally depend on @moe/core? (a) apps/daemon owns it and this task plans a loader plus a real call site; (b) the sibling keeps it and rail 2 is amended, or this task leaves the epic; (c) out of scope for M5, archive.

UNBLOCK on a human naming (a), (b) or (c). Not on re-measurement.

Confirmed the gap is total in both directions: zero hits for approvalMode/speedModeDelayMs anywhere in apps/packages/adapters, and zero for ProjectSettings/settingsDecode/decodeSettings/OrchestratorSettings, so nothing landed under another name. Additionally RULED OUT both candidate surfaces by name and line so they are not re-measured a fourth time: ProjectConfigurationSettings + parseProjectConfigurationSettings (packages/contracts/src/configuration/project-configuration-contract.ts:154, parser.ts:186) is the product manifest surface consumed by project-configuration-selection.ts for settingsDigest and carries no approval mode; WrapperKnobs + readWrapperKnobs (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts:9,32) are orchestrator ENV knobs. Re-blocked with the block reshaped from 'surface absent' to 'destination undecided'.
priorHandoffs.whatRemains: A human names one of three shapes: (a) apps/daemon owns the transitional settings load and auto-approval consumer, and this task then plans a loader PLUS a real call site there; (b) the sibling transitional daemon keeps ownership and epic rail 2 is amended to authorize the work, or this task leaves this epic; (c) transitional approval mode is out of scope for M5 and this task is archived. Only after that can this consumer be planned.
priorHandoffs.pitfalls: 1) DO NOT FILE A PREREQUISITE TASK TO 'unblock' this. The real consumer runs in the sibling transitional daemon and epic rail 2 pins development to moe-next, so a moe-next-local settings loader would land with no consumer here — the Clause-1 'exports the symbols is not composition' failure — and its owner could not satisfy their own consumer-edge DoD. Filing one is guessing the human's answer. 2) DO NOT re-run the three greps and call it progress; they stay zero until the decision is made, and this task has now consumed three architect passes doing exactly that. 3) Do not attach a standalone decoder to WrapperKnobs or to ProjectConfigurationSettings — measured, neither reaches transitional plan auto-approval. 4) Do not edit live .moe state or sibling-repo code under current epic rails.
priorHandoffs.openQuestions: The single blocking question, unanswered since architect-09b5f32a raised it on 2026-08-15: which repository/package is intended to own the real transitional settings load and auto-approval consumer, and how may it legally depend on @moe/core? Note the irony worth surfacing to the human: this board is itself running under approvalMode SPEED with speedModeDelayMs 2000, so the setting is live in the transitional daemon while being wholly unrepresented in moe-next source — which is precisely the migration question that needs deciding.
